items.title: Index
items.text:
jsonl

Zero-dependency Python library for reading, writing, and compressing JSON Lines files. 

import jsonl

jsonl.dump([{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}], "file.jsonl.gz")

for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl.gz"):
    print(item)

If you know json.dump and json.load, you already know jsonl.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Familiar API — same dump/load interface as Python's json module.
  • Streaming by default — iterators in, iterators out. Constant memory.
  • Automatic compression — .gz, .bz2, .xz, .zst (Python ≥ 3.14). Detected by extension or magic bytes.
  • Archive support — read/write .zip, .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz natively.
  • URL loading — pass a URL to load() or load_archive() directly.
  • Pluggable serialization — swap in orjson, ujson, or any encoder/decoder via cls.
  • Error tolerance — skip malformed lines instead of crashing.
  • Zero dependencies — pure standard library; single .py file you can vendor.

Fully compliant with the JSON Lines and NDJSON specifications.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install py-jsonl

Note

Requires Python 3.8+. No external dependencies.

items.title: Write and read
items.text:
import jsonl

# Write to plain or compressed files
jsonl.dump([{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}], "users.jsonl")
jsonl.dump([{"key": "value"}], "data.jsonl.gz")

# Read (lazy iterator — constant memory)
for user in jsonl.load("users.jsonl"):
    print(user)

# Read from a URL
for item in jsonl.load("https://example.com/data.jsonl"):
    print(item)

items.title: Archives
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    ("users.jsonl", [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}]),
    ("orders.jsonl", [{"id": 1, "total": 99.90}]),
]
jsonl.dump_archive("data.tar.gz", data)

for filename, items in jsonl.load_archive("data.tar.gz"):
    for item in items:
        print(filename, item)

items.title: Custom serialization
items.text:
import orjson
import jsonl

data = [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}]

jsonl.dump(data, "fast.jsonl", text_mode=False, cls=orjson.dumps)

for item in jsonl.load("fast.jsonl", cls=orjson.loads):
    print(item)

items.title: Reading
items.text: Function Description jsonl.load File, URL, or file-like → lazy iterator jsonl.loads JSON Lines string → lazy iterator jsonl.load_archive Unpack JSONL files from ZIP/TAR archive jsonl.loader Low-level line-stream deserializer

items.title: Writing
items.text:
Function Description jsonl.dump Write to file (any format) jsonl.dumps Serialize to string jsonl.dump_fork Write to multiple files at once jsonl.dump_archive Pack into ZIP/TAR archive jsonl.dumper Low-level generator → formatted lines

Custom Serialization

All functions accept cls and **kwargs for custom encoding/decoding.

items.title: Supported Formats
items.text:
Type Extensions Plain .jsonl Compressed .jsonl.gz · .jsonl.bz2 · .jsonl.xz · .jsonl.zst¹ ZIP .zip TAR .tar · .tar.gz · .tar.bz2 · .tar.xz · .tar.zst¹

¹ Requires Python ≥ 3.14

Info

When reading, if the file extension is not recognized, jsonl falls back to magic-number detection to identify the compression format automatically.

items.title: jsonl.dump
items.text: Write an iterable of objects to a JSON Lines file. Supports filenames (with automatic compression), os.PathLike objects, and file-like objects with write or writelines methods.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.dump(
    iterable,
    file,
    *,
    opener=None,
    text_mode=True,
    cls=None,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description iterable Iterable[Any] (required) Iterable of JSON-serializable objects file str, PathLike, file-like (required) Destination file path or file-like object opener Callable or None None Custom function to open the file (used only when file is a path) text_mode bool True If False, write bytes instead of text cls type[json.JSONEncoder] Callable or None json.JSONEncoder Custom encoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls encoder

items.title: Raises
items.text: Exception Condition ValueError If the file object is missing both writelines and write methods

items.title: Compression Detection
items.text:
Note

Supported compression formats: .gz, .bz2, .xz, .zst (Python ≥ 3.14)

When a filename is provided, the compression format is determined by its extension. If the extension is not recognized, the file is written as plain text.

items.title: Write to a file
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")

items.title: Write to a compressed file
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl.gz")  # gzip
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl.bz2")  # bzip2
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl.xz")  # xz
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl.zst")  # zst

items.title: Write to an open file object
items.text:
Tip

Useful when you need fine-grained control over how the file is opened, or when appending to an existing file.

import gzip
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

# Text file
with open("file.jsonl", mode="wt", encoding="utf-8") as fd:
    jsonl.dump(data, fd, text_mode=True)

# Binary compressed file
with gzip.open("file.jsonl.gz", mode="wb") as fd:
    jsonl.dump(data, fd, text_mode=False)

items.title: Append to an existing file
items.text:
import gzip
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

# Append to a compressed file
with gzip.open("file.jsonl.gz", mode="ab") as fp:
    jsonl.dump(data, fp, text_mode=False)

# Append to an uncompressed file
with open("file.jsonl", mode="at", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    jsonl.dump(data, fp, text_mode=True)

items.title: Write to a custom file object
items.text:
Tip

The custom file object must implement a write or writelines method.

import jsonl


class MyWriter:
    """A custom file object with a writelines method."""

    def writelines(self, lines):
        for line in lines:
            print(line, end="")


data = [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}]

jsonl.dump(data, MyWriter(), text_mode=True)

items.title: Using custom JSON Encoder
items.text:
import datetime
import json

import jsonl


class ISODateEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime.date):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


data = [
    {"name": "Alice", "birthdate": datetime.date(2000, 1, 1)},
    {"name": "Bob", "birthdate": datetime.date(2005, 1, 1)}
]

#  Write using a custom encoder to serialize datetime objects as ISO strings
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl", cls=ISODateEncoder)

items.title: Using a third-party library
items.text:
orjson is a high-performance JSON library that returns bytes:

import orjson
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

# orjson returns bytes — set text_mode=False
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl", cls=orjson.dumps, text_mode=False)

items.title: Passing keyword arguments
items.text:
Extra keyword arguments are forwarded directly to the cls decoder:

import jsonl

data = [{"name": "Alice", "score": 9.5}, {"name": "Bob", "score": 7.2}]

# Compact output (minimal whitespace)
jsonl.dump(data, "compact.jsonl", separators=(",", ":"))

# Sorted keys for deterministic output
jsonl.dump(data, "sorted.jsonl", sort_keys=True)

items.title: jsonl.dump_archive
items.text: Write multiple JSON Lines files into a ZIP or TAR archive. Supports compressed TAR variants and custom serialization.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.dump_archive(
    path,
    data,
    *,
    opener=None,
    text_mode=True,
    dump_if_empty=True,
    cls=None,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description path str (required) Destination path for the archive file data Iterable[tuple[str, Iterable[Any]]] (required) Iterable of (relative_path, items) tuples opener Callable or None None Custom function to open the given file paths text_mode bool True If False, write bytes instead of text dump_if_empty bool True If False, don't create empty files or an empty archive cls type[json.JSONEncoder] Callable or None json.JSONEncoder Custom encoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls encoder

items.title: Returns
items.text: str or None — Path to the created archive file, or None if no items were written and dump_if_empty is False.

items.title: Supported Archive Formats
items.text:
Extension Format .zip ZIP .tar TAR (uncompressed) .tar.gz TAR + gzip .tar.bz2 TAR + bzip2 .tar.xz TAR + xz .tar.zst TAR + zst (Python ≥ 3.14)

Warning

If the archive already exists at the given path, it will be overwritten.

Note

  • Paths in the data argument must be relative. Absolute paths will raise a ValueError.
  • If data contains multiple items for the same path, they are appended to the corresponding file within the archive.

items.title: Create a ZIP archive
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    ("users.jsonl", [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]),
    ("orders.jsonl", [{"id": 1, "total": 99.90}, {"id": 2, "total": 45.00}]),
]

jsonl.dump_archive("archive.zip", data)

items.title: Create a compressed TAR archive
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    ("users.jsonl", [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}]),
    ("logs/activity.jsonl", [{"event": "login", "ts": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]),
]

jsonl.dump_archive("archive.tar.gz", data)

items.title: Compressed files inside the archive
items.text:
Individual files within the archive can also be compressed:

import jsonl

data = [
    ("file1.jsonl", [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]),
    ("path/to/file2.jsonl.gz", [{"name": "Charlie", "age": 35}]),
    ("file1.jsonl", [{"name": "Eve", "age": 28}]),  # Appends to file1.jsonl
]

jsonl.dump_archive("archive.zip", data)

items.title: Skip empty files
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    ("has_data.jsonl", [{"value": 1}]),
    ("empty.jsonl", []),  # This file won't be created
]

# With dump_if_empty=False, empty files and empty archives are skipped
result = jsonl.dump_archive("archive.zip", data, dump_if_empty=False)

items.title: jsonl.dump_fork
items.text: Write data to multiple JSON Lines files simultaneously. This is useful when you need to split data across different files based on some criteria, while minimizing memory usage through incremental writing.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.dump_fork(
    paths,
    *,
    opener=None,
    text_mode=True,
    dump_if_empty=True,
    cls=None,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description paths Iterable[tuple[str, Iterable[Any]]] (required) Iterable of (filepath, items) tuples opener Callable or None None Custom function to open the given file paths text_mode bool True If False, write bytes instead of text dump_if_empty bool True If False, don't create empty files cls type[json.JSONEncoder] Callable or None json.JSONEncoder Custom encoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls encoder

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
• If the same filepath appears multiple times, subsequent data is appended to the file.
  • Files can use compression extensions (.gz, .bz2, .xz, and .zst Python ≥ 3.14 ) and will be compressed accordingly.
  • When dump_if_empty=False, files with no data are not created.

items.title: Split data into separate files
items.text:
import jsonl


def generate_player_files():
    """Yield (filepath, records) tuples — one file per player."""

    data = [
        {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [{"hand": "straight", "card": "7♣"}]},
        {"name": "May", "wins": [{"hand": "two pair", "card": "9♠"}]},
        {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [{"hand": "three of a kind", "card": "A♦"}]},
    ]
    for player in data:
        yield (f"{player['name']}.jsonl", player["wins"])


jsonl.dump_fork(generate_player_files())
# Creates: Gilbert.jsonl (with 2 entries), May.jsonl (with 1 entry)

items.title: Write to multiple files with static data
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    ("users.jsonl", [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]),
    ("orders.jsonl", [{"id": 1, "total": 99.90}, {"id": 2, "total": 45.00}]),
    ("users.jsonl", [{"name": "Eve", "age": 28}]),  # Appends to users.jsonl
]

jsonl.dump_fork(data)

items.title: Custom serialization
items.text:
import orjson
import jsonl


def worker():
    yield ("numbers.jsonl", ({"value": 1}, {"value": 2}))
    yield ("strings.jsonl", iter(({"a": "1"}, {"b": "2"})))
    yield ("numbers.jsonl", [{"value": 3}])


# Using orjson for faster serialization
jsonl.dump_fork(worker(), cls=orjson.dumps, text_mode=False)

items.title: jsonl.dumper
items.text: Low-level generator that yields formatted JSON Lines strings (or bytes) from an iterable of objects. This is the building block used internally by jsonl.dump and jsonl.dumps.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text: jsonl.dumper(iterable, *, text_mode=True, cls=None, **kwargs)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description iterable Iterable[Any] (required) Iterable of JSON-serializable objects text_mode bool True If True, yield str lines; if False, yield bytes cls type[json.JSONEncoder] Callable or None json.JSONEncoder Custom encoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls encoder

items.title: Returns
items.text: Iterator[str | bytes] — A generator yielding one formatted line per object (including trailing newline).

items.title: Basic usage
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}]

for line in jsonl.dumper(data):
    print(repr(line))

Output:

'{"name": "Alice"}\n'
'{"name": "Bob"}\n'

items.title: Yield bytes
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"x": 1}, {"x": 2}]

for line in jsonl.dumper(data, text_mode=False):
    print(repr(line))

Output:

b'{"x": 1}\n'
b'{"x": 2}\n'

items.title: Stream to a custom destination
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"event": "click"}, {"event": "scroll"}]

# Write lines to stdout or any writable target
import sys
for line in jsonl.dumper(data):
    sys.stdout.write(line)

items.title: jsonl.dumps
items.text: Serialize an iterable of objects into a JSON Lines formatted string.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.dumps(
    iterable,
    *,
    cls=None,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description iterable Iterable[Any] (required) Iterable of objects to serialize cls type[json.JSONEncoder] Callable or None json.JSONEncoder Custom encoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls encoder

items.title: Returns
items.text: str — A string with one JSON object per line.

items.title: Basic usage
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"foo": 1}, {"bar": 2}]
result = jsonl.dumps(data)
print(result)

Output:

{"foo": 1}
{"bar": 2}

items.title: With custom serialization
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]

# Compact output
result = jsonl.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"))
print(result)

Output:

{"name":"Bob","age":25}

items.title: With sorted keys
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"z": 1, "a": 2}, {"m": 3, "b": 4}]

result = jsonl.dumps(data, sort_keys=True)
print(result)

Output:

{"a": 2, "z": 1}
{"b": 4, "m": 3}

• Python 3.8 or higher
  • No external dependencies — jsonl uses only the Python standard library

With uv (recommended):

Or with pip:

items.title: jsonl.load
items.text: Deserialize a JSON Lines source into an iterator of Python objects. Supports filenames, URLs, urllib.request.Request objects, and file-like objects.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text: jsonl.load(source, *, opener=None, broken=False, cls=None, **kwargs)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str, PathLike, URL, Request, file-like (required) The JSON Lines source to read from opener Callable or None None Custom function to open the file (not supported for URLs) broken bool False If True, skip malformed lines and log a warning instead of raising an exception cls type[json.JSONDecoder] or Callable or None json.JSONDecoder Custom decoder **kwargs Keyword arguments used to pass the Custom decoder (cls)

items.title: Returns
items.text: Iterator[Any] — An iterator yielding deserialized Python objects, one per line.

items.title: Compression Detection
items.text:
Note

Supported compression formats: .gz, .bz2, .xz, and .zst (Python ≥ 3.14)

The compression format is resolved using two strategies:

  1. By file extension — if the file has a recognized extension (.gz, .bz2, .xz, .zst Python ≥ 3.14 ), that format is used directly.
  2. By magic numbers — when the extension is not recognized, jsonl inspects the first bytes of the file (magic numbers) to auto-detect the compression format.

If neither method identifies a known format, the file is treated as uncompressed.

items.title: Load from a file path
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")

for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl"):
    print(item)

items.title: Load from a compressed file
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

# Write to a gzip-compressed file
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl.gz")

# Load automatically detects the compression format
for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl.gz"):

items.title: Load from an open file object
items.text:
Tip

Useful when you need to read from a custom source or control how the file is opened.

import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")

items.title: Load from a URL
items.text:
You can load JSON Lines directly from a remote URL. For custom request headers, use urllib.request.Request:

import urllib.request
import jsonl

# Load directly from a URL
for item in jsonl.load("https://example.com/file.jsonl"):
    print(item)

# Load using a custom request with headers
req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://example.com/file.jsonl",
    headers={"Accept": "application/jsonl"},
)
for item in jsonl.load(req):
    print(item)

items.title: Handle broken lines
items.text:
Warning

When broken=False (default), an exception is raised on the first malformed line. When broken=True, malformed lines are skipped and a warning is logged.

import jsonl

# Create a file with a broken JSON line
with open("file.jsonl", mode="wt", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write('{"name": "Gilbert"}\n')
    fp.write('{"name": "May", "wins": []\n')  # Missing closing brace
    fp.write('{"name": "Richard"}\n')

# Skip broken lines
for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl", broken=True):
    print(item)

Output:

WARNING:jsonl:Broken line at 2: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 2 column 1 (char 28)
{'name': 'Gilbert'}
{'name': 'Richard'}

items.title: Using a custom JSON Decoder
items.text:
import json

import jsonl


class UpperDecoder(json.JSONDecoder):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, object_hook=self.object_hook, **kwargs)

    def object_hook(self, obj):
        return {k.upper(): v for k, v in obj.items()}


data = [{"name": "Gilbert"}, {"name": "May"}]
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")

# Read using a custom decoder to convert all keys to uppercase.
for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl", cls=UpperDecoder):
    print(item)

items.title: Passing keyword arguments
items.text:
Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to the cls decoder.

For example, parse float values as decimal.Decimal:

import decimal
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins_avg": 2.5},
    {"name": "May", "wins_avg": 3.75},
]
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")

for item in jsonl.load("file.jsonl", parse_float=decimal.Decimal):
    print(item)
    # float values are now decimal.Decimal instances

items.title: Custom opener
items.text:
The opener parameter lets you control how the file is opened. For example, reading from a ZIP archive:

import zipfile
import jsonl

data = [
    {"name": "Gilbert", "wins": [["straight", "7♣"], ["one pair", "10♥"]]},
    {"name": "May", "wins": []},
]

# Create a ZIP archive containing a jsonl file
jsonl.dump(data, "file.jsonl")
with zipfile.ZipFile("data.zip", "w") as zf:
    zf.write("file.jsonl")


def opener(name, *args, **kwargs):
    zf = zipfile.ZipFile(name)
    return zf.open("file.jsonl")


for item in jsonl.load("data.zip", opener=opener):
    print(item)

items.title: jsonl.load_archive
items.text: Load multiple JSON Lines files from a ZIP or TAR archive incrementally.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.load_archive(
    file,
    *,
    pattern="*.jsonl",
    pwd=None,
    opener=None,
    broken=False,
    cls=None,
    chunk_size=64 * 1024,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description file str, PathLike, URL, Request, file-like (required) Archive file to load from pattern str "*.jsonl" Unix shell-style wildcard pattern to filter filenames inside the archive pwd bytes or None None Password to decrypt the archive (ZIP only) opener Callable or None None Custom function to open the file (not supported for URLs) broken bool False If True, skip malformed lines and log a warning chunk_size int 64 * 1024 The size (in bytes) of chunks when reading from a URL to avoid loading the entire file into memory at once. cls type[json.JSONDecoder] or Callable or None json.JSONDecoder Custom decoder **kwargs Keyword arguments used to pass the Custom decoder (cls)

items.title: Returns
items.text: Iterator[tuple[str, Iterator[Any]]] — An iterator of (filename, items) tuples, where items is an iterator of deserialized objects.

items.title: Supported Archive Formats
items.text:
• ZIP archives (.zip)
  • TAR archives (.tar), including compressed variants: .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz, .tar.zst (Python ≥ 3.14)

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• Load from local files or remote URLs
  • Filter files inside the archive using Unix shell-style wildcards
  • Support for compressed .jsonl files inside the archive (e.g., .jsonl.gz, .jsonl.bz2, .jsonl.xz, .jsonl.zst ( Python ≥ 3.14) ). Check compression detection for details.
  • ZIP archives with password protection
  • Graceful handling of malformed lines via the broken parameter

items.title: Load from a local archive
items.text:
import jsonl

for filename, items in jsonl.load_archive("archive.zip"):
    print(f"--- {filename} ---")
    for item in items:
        print(item)

items.title: Load from a remote archive (URL)
items.text:
You can load archives from a URL. For custom request headers, use urllib.request.Request:

import urllib.request
import jsonl

# Load directly from a URL
for filename, items in jsonl.load_archive("https://example.com/archive.zip"):
    print(f"--- {filename} ---")
    for item in items:
        print(item)

# Load using a custom request with headers
req = urllib.request.Request("https://example.com/archive.zip", headers={"Accept": "application/zip"})
for filename, items in jsonl.load_archive(req, chunk_size=128 * 1024):  # increase chunk size for larger files if needed
    print(f"--- {filename} ---")
    for item in items:
        print(item)

items.title: Filter files with pattern matching
items.text:
Use Unix shell-style wildcards to select specific files within the archive:

Pattern Matches *.jsonl All .jsonl files (default) users*.jsonl Files starting with users data/[ab]*.jsonl Files in data/ starting with a or b * All files

For more details, see the fnmatch documentation.

import jsonl

# Load only files matching a specific pattern
for filename, items in jsonl.load_archive("archive.zip", pattern="users*.jsonl"):
    print(f"--- {filename} ---")
    for item in items:
        print(item)

items.title: jsonl.loader
items.text: Low-level generator that deserializes a line stream into Python objects. This is the building block used internally by jsonl.load.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text: jsonl.loader(stream, broken, *, cls=None, **kwargs)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description stream iterable of str or bytes (required) Any iterable yielding one JSON line per iteration broken bool (required) If True, skip malformed lines and log a warning cls type[json.JSONDecoder] or Callable or None json.JSONDecoder Custom decoder **kwargs Keyword arguments passed to the Custom decoder (cls)

items.title: Returns
items.text: Iterator[Any] — An iterator yielding deserialized Python objects, one per line.

items.title: Deserialize from an in-memory list
items.text:
import jsonl

lines = ['{"name": "Alice"}\n', '{"name": "Bob"}\n']

for item in jsonl.loader(lines, False):
    print(item)

Output:

{'name': 'Alice'}
{'name': 'Bob'}

items.title: Deserialize bytes lines
items.text:
import jsonl

lines = [b'{"x": 1}\n', b'{"x": 2}\n']

for item in jsonl.loader(lines, False):
    print(item)

items.title: Skip malformed lines
items.text:
import jsonl

lines = ['{"valid": true}\n', 'not json\n', '{"also": "valid"}\n']

for item in jsonl.loader(lines, True):
    print(item)

Output:

{'valid': True}
{'also': 'valid'}

items.title: With a custom decoder
items.text:
import orjson
import jsonl

lines = [b'{"name": "Alice"}\n', b'{"name": "Bob"}\n']

for item in jsonl.loader(lines, False, cls=orjson.loads):
    print(item)

items.title: jsonl.loads
items.text: Deserialize a JSON Lines formatted string into an object iterator.

items.title: Function Signature
items.text:
jsonl.loads(
    text,
    *,
    broken=False,
    cls=None,
    **kwargs,
)

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Type Default Description text str (required) JSON Lines formatted string broken bool False If true, skip broken lines (only logging a warning) cls type[json.JSONDecoder] Callable or None json.JSONDecoder Custom decoder **kwargs Additional keyword arguments passed to the cls decoder

items.title: Returns
items.text: Iterator[Any] — An iterator yielding one deserialized object per line.

items.title: Basic usage
items.text:
import jsonl

text = '{"foo": 1}\n{"bar": 2}\n'
for item in jsonl.loads(text):
    print(item)

Output:

{'foo': 1}
{'bar': 2}

items.title: Roundtrip with dumps
items.text:
import jsonl

data = [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}]
text = jsonl.dumps(data)

for item in jsonl.loads(text):
    print(item)

Output:

{'name': 'Alice'}
{'name': 'Bob'}

items.title: Tolerant parsing
items.text:
import jsonl

text = '{"a": 1}\nnot json\n{"b": 2}\n'
result = list(jsonl.loads(text, broken=True))
print(result)

Output:

[{'a': 1}, {'b': 2}]
